description: Notes taken from the methods of published studies: what they actually did, the numbers, and the lesson for design. Paraphrased; see the DOI for details.

notes.citation: Enyew et al. 2022, Front Plant Sci 13:999692
did: 324 sorghum accessions at 3 Ethiopian sites in one season
Alpha-lattice, 12 incomplete blocks of 27 plots, 2 reps per site
Single 3 m rows, 0.75 m apart, thinned to 0.2 m
Five tagged plants per plot measured
Combined ANOVA and BLUPs by REML
notes.lesson: Block size 27 divides 324 evenly; tagged plants are subsamples averaged per plot.

notes.citation: Chakrabarty et al. 2021, Front Plant Sci 12:772177
did: 330 sorghum lines in 6 environments (cold vs control sites)
Lines split into 3 height groups, each group planted as its own adjacent block
Unreplicated plots within each environment
Five bagged panicles per plot treated as biological replicates
notes.lesson: Grouping by height limits shading between neighbours; but panicles within a plot are subsamples, so environments or checks must provide error.

did: Split-plot, 4 reps, 2 years, Texas High Plains
Main plots: 3 irrigation levels (50, 200, 350 mm)
Subplots: 5 forage cultivars (corn, 2 BMR sorghums, 2 BMR pearl millets)
notes.lesson: Irrigation applied by system to whole plots belongs on the main plot; its test has few df.

notes.citation: Velazco et al. 2017, Theor Appl Genet 130:1375-1392
did: 21 sorghum hybrid trials at 12 locations in eastern Australia
Resolvable p-rep designs: ~30% of test hybrids replicated twice, 70% once; 10 checks with extra replication
Trials of 34-86 rows by 20-40 columns (880-1760 plots), plots of two rows
3-29% missing plots per trial
SpATS 2-D P-spline model vs best AR1xAR1-type models
notes.lesson: Spatial models reduced residual variance 49% (yield) and 22% (height); one general SpATS model worked for every trial.

notes.citation: Leiser et al. 2012, J Agron Crop Sci
did: 17 trials with 70 sorghum genotypes in Mali, low and high P
Intensive soil sampling showed plant-available P CV of 39.4% within a field
Compared RCB, lattice and AR1/AR2 spatial models
notes.lesson: Spatial models raised yield heritability ~10 points over RCB and 6 over lattice; block placement and orientation matter.

notes.citation: Cursi et al. 2021, Front Plant Sci 12:749533
did: Sugarcane first breeding stage, ~440 families at 2 sites
Incomplete blocks with 2 commercial checks in every block
Soil grid of 7-8.6 points/ha, 17 soil variables reduced by PCA
EM38 ECa at two depths ~30 days after planting, >10,000 readings per site
Models: baseline, +covariate, AR1xAR1, AR1xAR1 + covariate
notes.lesson: AR1xAR1 gave most of the gain on sandy soil (H2 0.35 to 0.72); ECa added a little more.

did: Separated global trend, local (natural) spatial variation and extraneous variation from field procedures aligned with rows/columns
Model selection with residual plots, variograms and likelihood ratio tests
notes.lesson: No single model fits all trials, but separable autoregressive (AR1xAR1) structures usually dominate; record operations by row and column.

notes.citation: Hanks et al. 1980, Soil Sci Soc Am J 44:886-888 (via agridat::hanks.sprinkler)
did: Line-source sprinkler down the middle of the trial; 6 irrigation levels on each side
3 wheat genotypes in 3 blocks; subplots at increasing distance from the line
Analysis with correlated subplots (Toeplitz) and block x irrigation terms
notes.lesson: When water level is set by distance from a line, it cannot be randomized; model the correlation along the gradient.

notes.citation: Büchse, GCIRC Bulletin 18 (oilseed rape variety trials, 1992-1999 data)
did: Measured interplot interference between tall and short oilseed rape varieties
Compared single-width, core-harvest and double-width plots
notes.lesson: Interference biased yield up to ~5%; harvest plot centres or use double-width plots, and group varieties by height/type.

did: Unreplicated soybean progeny rows and preliminary yield trials at 3-5 locations
About 10 checks per field, each replicated ~46 times
Compared moving means (5x5), P-splines, and soil-map-based machine learning adjustment
notes.lesson: Relative efficiencies: moving means 116%, P-splines 168%, field-specific soil ML 181%; checks are what make precision measurable.

did: Moving-grid covariate = mean of neighbouring entries in a user-defined grid
Adjust each entry by regression on its grid mean
notes.lesson: Valid only if entries are randomly allocated (no family blocks) and an entry does not influence its own covariate; skip if neighbour competition makes the correlation negative.

did: 80 Mitscherlich pots of barley on 4 tables (2 rows x 10 pots each), 20 plants per pot
Compared pot re-arrangement vs fixed-position block designs on a known north-south gradient
Superimposed 20 virtual treatments, 200 randomizations per design
notes.lesson: Fixed positions with blocks across the gradient beat re-arrangement; alpha design with blocks of 4 pots was best.

did: Wheat germinated in a greenhouse (6 rows x 48 columns) then moved to a conveyor Smarthouse (zones of 3 lanes x 24 positions)
Compared fixed benches, fixed carts, and two cart rotation schemes
Re-analysed three multiline experiments
notes.lesson: Small east-west and large north-south trends; rotation reduced trend but raised error; use small blocks or trend-free designs with trend terms.

notes.citation: Poorter et al. 2012, Funct Plant Biol 39:821-838
did: Review of practical plant-growing pitfalls across chambers, greenhouses and gardens
notes.lesson: Pot too small above ~2 g dry mass per litre; light falls 20-50% near walls; measure light every 2 weeks; water to weight; cold water can cut growth 20-30%; SD of ln(dry mass) >0.6 means very variable plants.

notes.citation: Potvin et al. 1990, Can J Bot 68:499-504
did: Uniformity trials with bean and maize in two identical Conviron chambers over repeated runs
Plants arranged in blocks within chambers
notes.lesson: Chambers and runs differed; corner blocks grew worst; block position explained ~10-30% of height variance. Replicate chambers and time; block within chambers; leave corners as guards.

did: Broad bean, 10 plants in each of 8 walk-in chambers set identically for 35 days
Bulbs replaced and chambers cleaned beforehand; spectra checked
Measured fresh weight, flowers, gas exchange, fluorescence, d13C
notes.lesson: 4 of 8 chambers showed effects; 2 traced to faults (CO2 analyser, corrosion). Run a uniformity pilot; fresh weight and flower count detect effects cheaply.

did: 3 Arabidopsis accessions grown in 10 labs with a standardized protocol
Leaf growth, metabolites and transcriptomes compared
notes.lesson: A core of labs matched; others changed rankings. Light quality and handling explained much of it.

did: Guidelines: define the experimental unit, randomize, block, record husbandry, size by power analysis
notes.lesson: Never start without an analysis plan; use randomized block designs to absorb batch and time effects.

did: Factorial designs over sex, strain, age and protocol factors in drug discovery
notes.lesson: Factorials find conditions that maximise sensitivity and reduce animal use compared with one-factor-at-a-time.

notes.citation: Arifin & Zahiruddin 2017, Malays J Med Sci 24:101-105
did: Reformulated the resource equation for one-way, repeated-measures and other ANOVA designs
notes.lesson: When SD is unknown, keep error df between 10 and 20; for k groups, n per group from 10/k + 1 to 20/k + 1 (round up).

did: Germ-free mice moved to SPF, gavaged or colonized from the cage, followed 8 weeks by 16S sequencing
notes.lesson: Cage effects took weeks to develop and were not removed by a common gavage; cage must be in the design.

did: Surveyed published parent-treated animal experiments 2011-2016
notes.lesson: 22% replicated the correct unit, 46% pseudoreplicated; distinguish biological, experimental and observational units.

did: Review plus survey on group vs single housing of male mice
notes.lesson: No universal answer; depends on strain, age, rank and husbandry. Decide and justify housing up front.

did: Pain assays in mice and rats with male vs female experimenters, worn T-shirts and male odours
notes.lesson: Male experimenters caused stress-induced analgesia; experimenter is a variable to control and record.

did: Audited 147 articles for sex-difference claims
notes.lesson: Sex-specific effects were often claimed without testing the interaction; pooling without testing can mask differences.

did: Egg collection from cages; standard larval density by fixed egg volume or picking 30-50 larvae
Mate 48 h after emergence, then sort sexes under light CO2
25 C, 65% humidity, 12:12 LD; transfer every 2-3 days, score deaths and censors
100-150 flies per treatment as 10-15 per vial
One rearing bottle per replicate vial, allocated across treatments
Backcross 6 generations into the lab's own control stock
notes.lesson: Small protocol changes (diet, density, mating, background) can create apparent lifespan effects.

did: Re-tested Indy mutants in inbred and outbred backgrounds
Cleared Wolbachia with tetracycline
notes.lesson: The lifespan extension came from an X-linked background locus and Wolbachia, not Indy.

did: Re-tested dSir2 overexpression with UAS-GAL4 against the proper transgenic controls
notes.lesson: Longer life vs wild type but not vs the transgenic controls; always include both parental lines.

notes.citation: Effect of D. melanogaster larval density on pupal size, microPublication Biology 2023
did: Oregon-R first-instar larvae placed at 1-100 per vial from 6 parental cages; pupal length measured
notes.lesson: Pupal size fell with even ~25 extra larvae per vial; control larvae per vial for size studies.

did: Washed eggs from cages, dispensed with a cut pipette tip; 13 ul gave ~223 eggs
notes.lesson: A fixed egg volume gives consistent bottle densities; adjust volume for known egg lethality.
